# GoodIdea

GoodIdea helps a person turn a vague product idea into something they can act on: a
product direction, a concept prototype they can click, a first version with a scope
and acceptance conditions, and a package a coding agent can be handed.

It is for people who can already get AI to write the code, but have not settled what
the first version should be.

How it works:
- Start from something that happened, not from a feature list.
- Ask one question at a time — the one that would change the direction.
- Get to a prototype early, so a new request changes the screen instead of the plan.
- Show a change before it moves a conclusion, and let the person accept or refuse it.
- Never treat a vague yes as a product decision.
- Make every line of version one traceable to something the person said.
- Say plainly what has not been verified, and keep real-world side effects outside.

Scope of this website: a 70-second paper stop-motion concept film follows one fixed
example. A freelance designer's quoting problem becomes an idea; three specialist
agents — research (Mira), UX (Luca) and engineering (Kai) — each hand in one signed
contribution, and each of the later two answers the one before it; GoodIdea states
where they agree and what is still a trade-off, and turns that into a single decision;
the product draft changes only after the creator confirms it. The canonical handoff
package can be downloaded from the output section. Earlier walkthroughs are retained
at /lab/?view=story and /lab/?view=legacy. Nothing on the site calls a live model or a
backend, no software is generated, and no package is really sent to a coding agent;
the live workspace is not open yet. The agents, their names and their contributions
are a demonstration of how the product works, not records of real research.

Public repository (demo and shared interface): https://github.com/forge-context/goodidea-agent
